transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you for fitting me in. Is it okay if I sit here? Great, thank you. 

Um, well, to be honest, I'm not entirely sure I need to be here, but I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing, and my wife thought it might be good for me to talk to someone. I hope I'm not taking up time from someone who needs it more. 

It's just... well, we've been having a bit of tension lately. Nothing major, I hope, just some confusion on my end. It's about her schedule. I know she says the late meetings and these... little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff. And I really do want to be reasonable and supportive about it. But for the past year, they’ve just lined up too precisely to feel completely accidental. 

It’s sort of... well, it feels like there’s a private signal in them, you know? Like they're meant to tell me something she won’t say directly. I know that probably sounds a bit strange to say out loud, doesn't it? I just want to make sure I'm looking at this the right way.
Besides these suspicions about your wife's messages, have you noticed anything unusual, like hearing voices or sounds other people don't seem to hear, or seeing things that others don't see?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I mean, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I'm... I'm completely fine in that regard, I promise. I know that kind of thing can be very serious, but I've never experienced anything like that. 

I'm just a normal guy, really. Just a teaching assistant trying to do a good job and be a good husband. It's really just this... this one thing with the messages that's been confusing me. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. I don't want to make it sound like I'm losing my mind or anything, because I'm definitely not hearing things. That's a good thing, right?
Aside from this concern about your wife's messages, how have things been going for you otherwise—your mood, your energy, your ability to concentrate at work, and your day-to-day functioning?

Oh, things are mostly fine, really. I mean, my mood is generally good. I'm still doing all my usual stuff. I show up for all my teaching sections on time, and I'm keeping up with the data analysis for my research group. I still ride my bike on the weekends, and I meet up with a couple of friends for chess every Thursday. I'm functioning perfectly normally, I promise. 

I guess... well, the only place it really gets a bit tricky is just at home. You know, when my wife and I get kind of stuck going in circles about what her schedule actually means. It can be a little exhausting, and I hate arguing with her. But other than that, everything is completely on track. Does that sound like what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how things are going.

Before this past year, would you say you've generally been a trusting person with friends, family, and coworkers, or have you often felt suspicious that other people were being deceptive or had hidden motives toward you, even back in your younger adult years?

Oh, no, I've always been very trusting. Honestly, probably too trusting sometimes! I've always gotten along really well with my family and my coworkers. I'm definitely not the kind of person who goes around looking for hidden motives or thinking people are out to get me. I've always believed in giving people the benefit of the doubt.

Even now, I don't think my wife is... well, I don't think she has malicious motives or anything like that. I really don't. It's just this one specific thing that's been confusing me. But generally speaking, no, I've never had issues trusting people. I've always had good, solid relationships. I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm some sort of paranoid person who suspects everyone, because that's really not who I am. Is that the kind of background information you needed?
